rules.name: Absolute Statutory Ban on Baby Walkers in Canada
rules.title: Absolute Statutory Ban on Baby Walkers in Canada
rules.directive_code: Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (CCPSA) Schedule 2, Item 15
rules.statute_citation: Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (CCPSA) Schedule 2, Item 15
rules.expected_requirement: CRIMINAL PROHIBITION: Baby walkers cannot be imported, advertised, or sold in Canada under any circumstances.
rules.explanation: Canada banned baby walkers in April 2004 under the Hazardous Products Act and reaffirmed it in Schedule 2 of the CCPSA. It is an offense to import or sell a baby walker in Canada, punishable by fines up to CAD $100,000 and imprisonment. Even if certified compliant to US ASTM F977 or European EN 1273, the product is 100% illegal in Canada.
rules.fix_suggestion: DO NOT IMPORT OR SHIP TO CANADA. Exclude Canada from shipping zones immediately.

rules.name: Mandatory English/French Bilingual Packaging & Description
rules.title: Mandatory English/French Bilingual Packaging & Description
rules.directive_code: Consumer Packaging and Labelling Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-38), Section 6
rules.statute_citation: Consumer Packaging and Labelling Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-38), Section 6
rules.expected_requirement: All mandatory label information (product identity, net quantity, instructions, warnings) must be displayed in both English and French with equal prominence.
rules.explanation: Federal Canadian law strictly mandates bilingual packaging across all provinces. Unilingual English labels are regularly stopped at CBSA ports of entry and subject to corrective labeling orders.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add accurate Canadian French translations alongside English text for all label declarations, instructions, and net quantity statements.

rules.name: Health Canada 3.0% Camphor Concentration Cap
rules.title: Health Canada 3.0% Camphor Concentration Cap
rules.directive_code: Health Canada Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist - Camphor Entry
rules.statute_citation: Health Canada Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist - Camphor Entry
rules.expected_requirement: Maximum 3.0% camphor in topical cosmetics. Concentrations exceeding 3% are prohibited for cosmetics.
rules.explanation: Health Canada's Hotlist restricts camphor in cosmetics to <= 3%. If camphor exceeds 3%, the formulation is classified as a Natural Health Product (NHP) or drug requiring an NPN license.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure camphor does not exceed 3.0% for cosmetic distribution in Canada, or apply for an NPN license.

rules.name: Natural Health Product (NHP) Licensing Requirement for Therapeutic Claims
rules.title: Natural Health Product (NHP) Licensing Requirement for Therapeutic Claims
rules.directive_code: Food and Drugs Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. F-27) Section 3 & Schedule A
rules.statute_citation: Food and Drugs Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. F-27) Section 3 & Schedule A
rules.expected_requirement: 8-digit Natural Product Number (NPN) and Canadian Site Licence required before importing products making health or therapeutic claims.
rules.explanation: Section 3 of the Food and Drugs Act prohibits advertising treatments for Schedule A conditions (such as arthritis) to the general public without Health Canada authorization.
rules.fix_suggestion: Remove disease claims to remain in the cosmetic category, or secure an 8-digit NPN license prior to commercial importation.

rules.name: Lithium Battery Air Transport Declaration
rules.title: Lithium Battery Air Transport Declaration
rules.directive_code: Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) Regulations / Transport Canada
rules.statute_citation: Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) Regulations / Transport Canada
rules.expected_requirement: Transport Canada TDG compliant shipping documentation and UN 38.3 testing verification.
rules.explanation: Dangerous goods regulations mandate verified testing and labeling for lithium battery consignments entering Canadian airspace.
rules.fix_suggestion: Provide battery test certificate and declare under TDG special provision 34.

rules.name: CCPSA Heavy Metals in Surface Coatings on Toys (Lead <= 90 mg/kg)
rules.title: CCPSA Heavy Metals in Surface Coatings on Toys (Lead <= 90 mg/kg)
rules.expected_requirement: Total lead content in surface coatings must not exceed 90 mg/kg (90 ppm). Mercury must not be intentionally added.
rules.explanation: Health Canada rigorously prosecutes and recalls toys with lead or heavy metal migration under CCPSA Section 23.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure surface coatings pass Health Canada Product Safety Reference Manual Method C-02.2 testing.

rules.name: Pest Control Products Act (PCPA) Treated Articles Policy
rules.title: Pest Control Products Act (PCPA) Treated Articles Policy
rules.directive_code: Pest Control Products Act (S.C. 2002, c. 28) / PMRA Regulatory Directive
rules.statute_citation: Pest Control Products Act (S.C. 2002, c. 28) / PMRA Regulatory Directive
rules.expected_requirement: Public health pathogen eradication claims require PMRA registration. Preservative antimicrobial claims are allowed only if preservative is registered under PCPA.
rules.explanation: Health Canada's PMRA prohibits claims that treated articles protect users against human pathogens without full drug/biocide registration.
rules.fix_suggestion: Rephrase antimicrobial claim to specify it only protects the product itself against odor and stain-causing bacteria, not human health pathogens.

rules.name: Mandatory Cosmetic Notification Form (CNF) Submission
rules.title: Mandatory Cosmetic Notification Form (CNF) Submission
rules.expected_requirement: Submission of a complete Cosmetic Notification Form (CNF) to Health Canada within 10 days of first commercial sale in Canada.
rules.explanation: Failure to notify Health Canada of cosmetic formulations and ingredient concentrations within 10 days of importation constitutes a regulatory violation leading to border stop orders.
rules.fix_suggestion: Submit online CNF notification via Health Canada's portal and verify all ingredients match INCI nomenclature.
